title: Norms
coreMove: Treat a norm as a rule backed by group enforcement, then ask what visible selfishness it makes costly.
sourcePressure: The source explains norms as collectively enforced rules that let groups suppress visible selfishness through coalition pressure, gossip, and reputation.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer treats norms as polite values instead of enforced social technology.

sourceAnchors.name: nomadic egalitarian groups of 20-50 members
sourceAnchors.detail: The source uses small hunter-gatherer groups of roughly 20-50 members to explain collective norm enforcement.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: In a band of 20 to 50 people, reputation is not background noise; it is the court.

sourceAnchors.name: weapons as coalition equalizers
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says weapons helped coalitions of weaker members enforce norms against stronger individuals.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A spear changes the politics of selfish strength when weaker people can stand together.

sourceAnchors.name: gossip and reputation enforcement
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names gossip and reputation as tools that help enforce norms.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The punishment often starts as talk before it becomes anything formal.

exampleSpecs.audience: a team lead stopping one strong member from taking extra equipment
exampleSpecs.stakes: the norm protects the whole team only if visible grabbing becomes costly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire places the sign-out tags on the table and asks every rescuer to read the missing harness numbers aloud before anyone confronts the strongest climber.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Mud flakes from the rope bag onto the gear-room floor.

exampleSpecs.audience: a tenant board dealing with a charming rule-bender
exampleSpecs.stakes: silent resentment is replacing enforceable standards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "He only takes Sundays because nobody uses them," Henrik says, and Paula turns the private complaints into a posted rotation everyone can verify.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "He only takes Sundays because nobody uses them," Henrik says at the tenant table.

exampleSpecs.domain: local running club race bib allocation
exampleSpecs.audience: a club treasurer protecting fair access to a scarce marathon entry
exampleSpecs.stakes: favor-currying could quietly decide who gets the entry
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Who gets the bib when the fastest runner also brought the sponsor?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Who gets the bib when the sponsor is standing beside the fastest runner?

exampleSpecs.audience: a captain preventing status from capturing scarce training
exampleSpecs.stakes: bragging and subgroup politics can split the brigade before fire season
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam moves the training list from the captain's truck window to a public board and requires two signatures for every swap.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The empty hook for the thermal camera sits above the training board.

exampleSpecs.audience: a chair stopping reputation deals from shaping grant rankings
exampleSpecs.stakes: review norms fail if whispered bargains stay below common knowledge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Aanya one leaked ranking to see that private praise had become currency, so she makes conflicts and prior favors visible before scoring begins.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Aanya one leaked ranking to reread every friendly email.

exampleSpecs.audience: a coach enforcing anti-bragging norms around ten-year-olds
exampleSpecs.stakes: a parent's visible self-promotion is teaching the team what the group tolerates
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You ask Nicolas to hand the player-of-the-week patch to the quiet defender he ignored, making the group reward the norm instead of the boast.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You hear the parent narrating his child's goal before the kids reach halftime.

skillTargets: identify which group sanction makes a norm real
distinguish a value statement from enforceable collective pressure
choose interventions that turn private irritation into shared enforcement without mobbing

tryThisNowSpec: Name one rule your group claims to hold. Write the actual sanction beside it: gossip, lost trust, exclusion, formal penalty, or nothing.
